exercise.name: Dumbbell Bar Grip Sumo Squat
aliases: Wide-stance dumbbell squat holding the handle

reference.title: Dumbbell Bar Grip Sumo Squat
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, lower; breathe out as you stand.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, a pause at the bottom, then stand on two low steps for more depth. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Wide stance, toes turned out. Hold one dumbbell across your body by the handle with both hands, overhand, hands side by side, arms long.
Breathe in, brace, push the knees out over the toes and sit straight down; the dumbbell hangs between the legs.
Thighs about parallel, chest up, arms long, heels down.
Squeeze the glutes and drive up; breathe out near the top.

mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the toes all the way down and up.
Arms stay long and relaxed; only the legs move it.
Keep the chest up; the dumbbell hangs straight under the shoulders.
Shoulders down and back; let the arms hang.

kinematics.norm: About 1.4-2x shoulder width; 140% of shoulder width was the widest stance in McCaw 1999, about 1.7x acromion width in Larsen 2021
About 30-45 degrees, matched to the knees (Lorenzetti 2018; Sinclair 2022)
About 100-120 degrees at thighs parallel (clinical opinion; Larsen 2021 reported about 119-120 degrees in wide-stance loaded squats)
Not specified by the sources for this load and trunk angle
Held across by the handle, hanging at arm length between the legs (common coaching)
About 2 s down, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #9339, Dumbbell Bar Grip Sumo Squat, video (movement reference)
McCaw & Melrose 1999, stance width and bar load effects on leg muscle activity during the parallel squat (Med Sci Sports Exerc 31:428-436)
Larsen et al. 2021, stance width and bar placement in back squats: kinematics, kinetics and EMG (Front Sports Act Living)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)
Sinclair et al. 2022, habitual and manipulated foot angles in the barbell back squat (Sensors)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Groin or hip discomfort: narrow the stance a little and turn the toes out less.
progressions: Feet on two low steps for more depth.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; stance width did not change quadriceps activity (McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; stance width did not change quadriceps activity (McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor; a wide stance changed buttock muscle activity compared with narrower stances (McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor; a wide stance changed buttock muscle activity compared with narrower stances (McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Medial thigh muscles work harder with the wide stance (McCaw 1999 found stance width changed medial thigh activity).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Medial thigh muscles work harder with the wide stance (McCaw 1999 found stance width changed medial thigh activity).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees pushed out over the turned-out toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees pushed out over the turned-out toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall over the wide base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up; the wide stance lets the trunk stay more upright (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up; the wide stance lets the trunk stay more upright (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle overhand for the whole set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handle overhand for the whole set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level while the dumbbell hangs from the arms (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level while the dumbbell hangs from the arms (clinical opinion).
